_COMMENT: PLACEHOLDER. NOT A SHIPPABLE MOD METADATA FILE.
This file exists only so the resource layout of `core` matches what a loader will
eventually expect, and so the JSON is parsed by something rather than rotting.
The REAL `fabric.mod.json` belongs to the platform modules (platform-1.8.9 and
platform-1.21.11), because it must declare one entrypoint per pole and each pole
pins a different loader, different mappings and a different Fabric API line.
`core` is a plain java-library: it is not a mod and is never loaded by a game.
Jar-in-JAR wiring (`jars` / `include`, used to bundle Fabric API into our mod) comes
with the platform modules too. Fabric API is version-keyed per Minecraft version and
cannot be bundled once for both poles.
What eventually lands here per pole: schemaVersion, id, version, name, environment,
entrypoints -> the pole's XsozClientPlatform, depends -> fabric-api for that pole,
custom -> minLauncherVersion, and the META-INF/services entry that names the single
PlatformAdapter implementation. Nothing above is written yet.
name: XsozClient Core (PLACEHOLDER - NOT A MOD)
description: Pure-Java core library. This metadata file is a placeholder; the shipped mod metadata lives in the platform modules.
